newsitem.title: USA: Committee back Transportation secretary nominee.
newsitem.headline: Committee back Transportation secretary nominee.

text.p: The Senate Commerce Committee Wednesday unanimously endorsed Rodney Slater to be secretary of Transportation during President Clinton's second term.
The full Senate may confirm Slater as early as Thursday, Senate Commerce Committee Chairman John McCain, R-Arizona, said after the panel approved the nominee by voice vote.
Slater, 41, has been head of the Transportation Department's Federal Highway Administration, which oversees the U.S. highway system, since 1993.
He would succeed Federico Pena as secretary of the department. Pena has been nominated by Clinton to be energy secretary.

Slater, from Marianna, Arkansas, has been a political ally of Clinton since the president was governor of Arkansas. He was named by Clinton to the Arkansas Highway Commission and later became its first black chairman.

The Senate has confirmed four of Clinton's second term nominations: Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, Defence Secretary William Cohen, Commerce Secretary William Daley and Housing and Urban Development Secretary Andrew Cuomo.

Other pending nominations, in addition to Pena and Slater, include Alexis Herman to be secretary of Labour, Anthony Lake to be director of the Central Intelligence Agency and Janet Yellen to chair the Council of Economic Advisers.
